text:
violet: Found weird behavior in the Next + LangChain starter: when wiring the LlamaIndex connector and using the SDK client retry middleware, some prompts are being sent twice to the model (duplicate tokens billed) and the eval harness reports inflated latency. Anyone else seeing duplicate /generate calls?
sam: Repro'd locally. Steps: clone starter, set RW_KEY, yarn dev, POST /api/chain with body. Network trace shows two POSTs to /generate with identical payloads and no idempotency header. Looks like retry middleware retries on 429/timeout but the adapter doesn't attach an idempotency token so the server executes twice.
andy: This also breaks the eval harness JSON diff: it expects single output but we get duplicated outputs which are treated as regressions. I see `WARN: duplicate inference detected` in harness logs.
violet: Minimal mitigation: add `x-rw-idempotency` header generated per logical request and make the SDK retry middleware only resend for connection errors (not for 4xx/429 unless we know server didn't start processing). I'll open a small PR to the starter showing the pattern.
sam: I'll implement `getIdempotency()` util and update the starter to pass that header from Next API handler -> sdk client call. Also adding a tiny unit test asserting a single /generate call is recorded by the harness when the server returns a 429 then succeeds.
ci-bot: created issue DE-599: "next-starter: duplicate model calls due to retry middleware + eval harness false-positives" assigned to @sam @andy.
andy: For short-term onboarding, add a README note recommending `RW_RETRY_MODE=optimistic` or recreating the client per-request to avoid cached retry state.
violet: Good. Longer-term: SDK could expose a safeRetry wrapper or idempotency helper so sample apps don't have to implement this themselves.
sam: PR #150 opened with starter patch and e2e job in GH Actions that asserts one /generate per input. Requesting reviews.
violet: Thanks — once merged, patch the quickstart generator so new users pick up the fix and we reduce lead friction for first-run evals.
